assessmentPoints: Centripetal force answers in the centre-seeking push activity
successCriteria: F = mv^2/r = 1200 x 225 / 50 = 5400 N, directed toward the centre of the bend (supplied by friction).
objectives.text: Explain why circular motion needs a centripetal force toward the centre and compute it with F = mv^2/r

assessmentPoints: Gravitation answers in the gravity holds the Moon activity
successCriteria: It would fall to one quarter, from F = GMm/r^2 with r doubled
F = GMm/r^2. The gravitational attraction toward the Earth is itself the centripetal force holding the Moon on its circular path.
objectives.text: Use Newton's law of gravitation F = GMm/r^2 as the centripetal force for orbits

assessmentPoints: Geostationary answers in the geostationary orbits activity
Trap answers in the toolkit activity
successCriteria: The orbit must be above the equator and travel in the same direction as the Earth's rotation (west to east). With period 24 hours and the same angular speed as the Earth, the satellite stays over the same point on the equator and appears fixed.
No outward fling exists: the body wants to keep going straight while the seat pushes it inward - the inward push is the real force
objectives.text: State the conditions for a geostationary orbit and avoid the centrifugal fling-off trap
